english.title: Carry / remove / deposit / conceal etc goods with intent to defraud His Majesty
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) was knowingly concerned in

(A)_[carrying]_
(B)_[removing]_
(C)_[depositing]_
(D)_[harbouring]_
(E)_[keeping]_
(F)_[concealing]_
(G)_[dealing with]_
(H)_[**(..WHERE MORE THAN ONE OF THE ABOVE OPTIONS APPLY - SPECIFY..)]_

certain goods, namely **(..SPECIFY THE NATURE OF THE GOODS..), which

(I)_[had been unlawfully removed from a warehouse or a King's warehouse]_
(J)_[were chargeable with a duty which had not been paid]_

with intent to defraud His Majesty of any duty payable on the goods
english.legislation: Contrary to section 170(1)(b), and (3) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.

investigatoraction.description: Criminal lifestyle offence under Schedule 2 to POCA - consider confiscation order

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See offence wordings H3639 and H3640 for import / export - fraudulent evasion of duty / prohibition.
(ii) See section 171 for general provisions as to offences and penalties.
(iii) See section 49 for forfeiture provisions
(iv) Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the offences to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.
